references.text: Aaron cast lots over the two goats, one lot for the Lord and the other for Azazel. This verse explains how the lots were cast before the goat was presented.
The goat as a sin offering for the people was slaughtered, and its blood was brought inside the veil. This shows the completion of the sin offering that began in verse 9.
Instructions regarding the sin offering (חַטָּאת) for the priest, showing the general law of the sin offering that Aaron was to perform.
The sin offering was to be slaughtered at the place where the burnt offering was slaughtered, before the Lord's presence. This is parallel to the sin offering on the Day of Atonement.
Aaron presented the people's sin offering on the day of consecration, which parallels his service on the Day of Atonement.
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for himself and for the sins of the people. This points back to Aaron's service on the Day of Atonement.
Christ entered the holy place with his own blood and secured eternal redemption. The sin offering on the Day of Atonement was a foreshadowing of Christ's sacrifice.
